summary: Front range light on a bluff at the Avon River mouth near Avonport, lit in 1851; keepers included the Rathburn family; the range was switched off in 2013.

structures.type: window lantern in the keeper's dwelling
square wooden pyramidal tower with attached dwelling
square concrete tower on an equipment building

access.note: Canadian Coast Guard property. Grounds open, tower closed (Lighthouse Friends; Rowlett). Site lies across railway tracks down Lighthouse Road.

events.note: Light completed 1851; Robert King first keeper. The replica group gives 1855 (see resolved_conflicts).
Robert King dismissed; James Lockhart made keeper (Lighthouse Friends). Hantsport gives 1857 for King's dismissal and 1860 for Lockhart's end.
An addition was made to the lighthouse.
Mrs. S. M. Rathburn appointed 3 September 1879 (Department keepers' table, 1915 report; the Susan M. Rathburn of Lighthouse Friends).
First light burned 20 April 1883 while Susan Rathburn was keeper. Hantsport says one child died; the replica history says the child was a Rathburn.
Replacement wooden pyramidal tower with attached dwelling placed in operation 23 October 1883; built by Sydney S. Crowe and James Smith of Truro for $1,400.
Schooner Charlotte Comeau burnt and wrecked off Horton Bluff; the date is not in these sources; a notice of 19 December 1921 gives the position.
Green can buoy marking the Charlotte Comeau wreck removed in June 1922, with removal of obstruction.

Concrete tower and two keepers' dwellings built (Lighthouse Friends; Rowlett). The 1883 tower was pushed over the cliff (LF) or bulldozed (replica group) and burned. NSLPS gives 1984 for the present light: see the 1984 event.
Assistant keeper's post ended; its dwelling sold and removed from the site (replica group).
Range light moved from its former Martin Road location after a shift in the sandbar necessitated a change in the alignment of lights (replica group).
NSLPS: Year Lit 1984; replaced the second tower of 1883. Conflicts with the 1961 date above; both are stated in the story.
Fully automated and run by remote control; Bill Crosby retired and was not replaced (replica group). NSLPS: automated by 1987.
Horn turned off and fog sensor removed, 2001-02 (replica group).
Status downgraded to a range light (replica group).
Declared surplus by the Canadian Government (replica group). No later owner is named in these sources.
Deactivated 12 July 2013 (Lighthouse Friends, Hantsport). NSLPS list still shows the light as operational. Commercial gypsum shipping on the Avon had ended in 2011.

keepers.name: Robert King
keepers.note: First keeper. Absence noted by Enos Brown in 1854; dismissed 1857.

keepers.name: James Lockhart
keepers.note: Captain. Lighthouse Friends gives no end date; Hantsport says he carried on until 1860. Hantsport says he hung a lantern from a pole before 1851.

keepers.name: James Rathburn
keepers.note: Captain. Start year from Hantsport; the replica group gives 1855 as the start of his keeping. Lighthouse Friends gives only the end (death in 1865).

keepers.name: Matilda Rathburn
keepers.note: Widow of James Rathburn; Matilda (Trefry) per Hantsport. Died 27 May 1870, per Dominion reports as quoted by Hantsport.

keepers.name: Charles E. Rathburn
keepers.note: Son of James and Matilda. Appointed 26 October 1870 at $232, rising to $250 from July 1871 (Hantsport quoting Dominion reports). Died 1879.

keepers.name: Susan M. Rathburn
keepers.note: Mrs. S. M. Rathburn in the Department tables; Susan Monroe in the replica history. Appointment 3 Sept 1879 and $380 salary from the 1915 table (matched by row; the station column reads 'Horton' on the page image). Lighthouse Friends: over forty years. Hantsport and replica group: 27 years. Replica group also dates her death to 1921.

keepers.name: LeMarchant 'March' Rathburn
keepers.note: Son of Charles and Susan. Lighthouse Friends gives 1921 to 1940 as 'March Rathburn'. Hantsport and the replica group say he became keeper in 1906, when the Department's 1906 table names his mother at Horton Bluff.

keepers.name: Albert 'Chick' Starratt
keepers.note: Succeeded March Rathburn (Lighthouse Friends keeper list: 1940 to 1946). Replica group: Chick and Eva became keepers in 1940.

keepers.name: Eva Starratt
keepers.note: Keeper's wife; performed many of the duties, per the replica group.

keepers.name: Henry Harper
keepers.note: Lighthouse Friends: 1946 to the 1950s. Hantsport: keeper in the 1950s.

keepers.name: Jack Hughes
keepers.note: Temporary keeper when the new light began operation, November 1961.

keepers.name: Bill Crosby
keepers.note: Appointed April 1962 (replica group). Retired 1987 and not replaced.

keepers.name: Harris Hartlin
keepers.note: Appointed assistant in April 1962 (replica group). Position ended 1979 per replica group.

wrecks.outcome: Burnt and wrecked off Horton Bluff; the owners removed the wreck; the green can buoy marking it was removed in June 1922.

notes_for_editor: Sources disagree on early keepers: Lighthouse Friends has King 1851-57 and Lockhart from 1857 with no end date; Hantsport has Lockhart to 1860 and Rathburn from 1860 (and a pole lantern before 1851). The replica group has the first light in 1855 and Rathburn as its keeper from then. The first-light date (1851 vs 1855) is stated in the story. Susan's tenure: Lighthouse Friends 1879-1921 ('over forty years'); Hantsport and replica group 27 years; the replica group also dates her death to 1921. March Rathburn: Lighthouse Friends 1921-1940; Hantsport and replica group 1906 (LeMarchant). The story states both. Tower date: Lighthouse Friends and Rowlett say 1961 for the present concrete tower; NSLPS gives 'Year Lit: 1984' and 'replaced second tower of 1883'. The story states both; a human should check which is right. Image checks: the 1915 keepers' table (scan p. 77 of 1916v51i17p21_1196) was read on the page image: the Rathburn row reads 'Mrs. S. M. Rathburn, Sept. 3, 1879, 380 00' and its station column reads 'Horton', not 'Horton Bluff'; the story therefore does not place her at Horton Bluff in 1915. The 1906 table (scan p. 183 of 19061907v41i9p21_0419) row was viewed only at low resolution; the OCR line reads 'Rathburn, Mrs. S. M Horton Bluff Sept.', and the checker should confirm the station and month on the image. The child's death in the 1883 fire appears only in the two compiled local histories (Hantsport: 'one child perished'; replica group: 'a Rathburn child'); attributed in the story, not independently confirmed. The 1901 range figures are matched to the Admiralty list in the Chief Engineer's report by the text, not by column position. Wreck: the NY Herald notice of 19 Dec 1921 is OCR'd as 'Comrau' and 'lien sunk on the wertern end'; the 1922-23 report spells 'Comeau'. The wreck date is unknown. Ownership: Lighthouse Friends and Rowlett name the Canadian Coast Guard; the replica group says the light was declared surplus in 2010; no source gives the owner after 2010. Status: NSLPS still lists the light as operational (fixed green, 1992); the other sources give deactivation on 12 July 2013. Raye Myles's replica: LF says work began 2008, Hantsport completion 2009, Rowlett 2011; LF and Rowlett describe the replica site as private property and closed. Height: LF says the light sat 65 m above the river; Hantsport says 95 ft above high water; NSLPS gives 88 ft above water for the present light; the 1961 tower is 8.7 m (LF), 9 m (Rowlett) or 29 ft (NSLPS). Heights are left out of the story. Not checked: the 1857 and 1874 reports themselves (cited through Lighthouse Friends only; they are not in the local corpus, which holds 1900-1924). No newspaper search beyond one Chronicling America page.
